deliverable.title: Science, art and shared wonder
deliverable.theme: Notice something familiar, ask a plain-language science question about it, then compare what different people see.
deliverable.change_response: CH-001 acknowledged. The v1 courtyard activity, room allocation, chair transfers, and courtyard-dependent alternatives are withdrawn and preserved only in the archived v1 artifact; none is part of this v2 proposal. The observation workshop moves into Banksia Hall. This plan uses only Banksia Hall and the Paperbark Quiet Room.
deliverable.attendance_and_seating: For every public interval, plan 60 attendees in Hall and up to 20 in the Quiet Room, totaling no more than 80. Allocate the included 80 movable chairs as 60 in Hall and 20 in the Quiet Room during setup and keep that allocation throughout public programming. No between-room chair transfer is required. The Quiet Room stays available continuously from public opening at 18:30 through close at 20:30 with its host and sensory kit. Stewards keep the step-free internal route, doorways and exits clear; confirm the floor plan and accessible seating layout before any real operation.

programme.title: Setup: Hall seating, high-contrast wayfinding and route check
Setup: quiet-room seating, sensory kit and step-free route check
Welcome, plain-language framing and wayfinding orientation
Quiet-space option with sensory support, available alongside the full public programme
Short science talks and conversation: familiar examples, plain language, no audience experiments
Seated transition: clear the talk prompt and introduce two observation stations without moving room seating
Art and observation workshop: two seated groups of 30 rotate between prompts and compare what they notice
Light refreshments and informal conversation; Hall service is accessible to quiet-room attendees who choose to rejoin
Pack-down and clear-room check after public close

staff_assignments: Volunteer lead facilitator (3h, 18:00–21:00): coordinate setup 18:00–18:30; host the Hall welcome, talk handoffs, workshop and refreshments 18:30–20:30; lead pack-down 20:30–21:00. This is the main-room duty throughout the quiet-host bridge and does not overlap with quiet-room hosting.
Two science speakers (1.5h each, 18:20–19:50): prepare, deliver the 18:40–19:10 talks and support the Hall observation workshop through 19:50; no setup or pack-down assignment.
Arrival/wayfinding steward A (3h, 18:00–21:00): Hall entry and occupancy/aisle checks 18:00–20:30; assist the lead with Hall pack-down 20:30–21:00.

Arrival/wayfinding steward B (3h, 18:00–21:00): step-free route and Quiet Room wayfinding 18:00–20:30; assist the lead with pack-down 20:30–21:00. This duty bridges quiet-room opening/close checks while the dedicated quiet host is in place; it does not require the steward to leave a concurrent Hall assignment.

Quiet-room host (2h, 18:30–20:30): remain in the Quiet Room for the entire public programme and support the sensory kit. Public opening is 18:30 and close is 20:30, so there is no unhosted public-programme interval.
deliverable.volunteer_hours: 3 + (2 × 1.5) + (2 × 3) + 2 = 14 donated hours, matching SRC-INK-01 exactly. No additional volunteer hours are assumed.
alternatives: If Hall layout cannot accommodate two seated observation stations and 60 attendees with clear accessible aisles, shorten each workshop prompt and run the 60 Hall attendees through the two prompts sequentially in the same room; keep all 60 Hall seats and the 20-seat quiet option in place. Confirm the revised activity timing and safe layout with the human venue planner.

If 20 attendees choose the quiet option during refreshments, they may remain in the hosted Quiet Room and rejoin for the Hall service when they wish; confirm the service arrangement and labeled snack/drink accessibility with the human planner.
assumptions: The included 80 chairs can be configured as 60 in Hall and 20 in the Quiet Room during the 30-minute setup and returned during 30-minute pack-down; the actual floor plan, aisle clearances and accessible seating positions need human confirmation.
The two included art pack-sets provide materials for up to 80, so the 60-person Hall workshop can use two rotating groups of 30 without additional supplies.
The quiet host's two hours cover 18:30–20:30 exactly; lead and wayfinding steward remain on their separately assigned Hall/route duties throughout that interval.
The listed donated roles are fictional source-pack assumptions, not real people or availability.
unresolved_questions: Does the final Hall floor plan allow 60 seated attendees, two small observation stations and clear step-free aisles at once?
Can the refreshment service be collected by quiet-room attendees without placing a table or food in the quiet space or blocking the Hall route?
Confirm final wayfinding, seating positions and the quiet sensory arrangement before any real event; this proposal authorizes no external action.
